items.title: Fourteen of 20 banks now offer reducing balance hire-purchase financing, says Armizan
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — Fourteen of the 20 banking institutions providing hire-purchase financing had begun offering customers the reducing balance method as of Sept 18, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. He said the remaining six banking institutions are expected to complete the transition to the new method by December 31 at the latest, following engagement sessions with the banks. According to Armizan, the amendments to the Act that took effect on June 1 introduced the reducing balance method and effective interest rate, replacing the flat interest rate and “Rule of 78” method.

items.title: Melaka PH, Bersatu in talks to form 'PH Plus' for state election
items.summary: MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan is finalising negotiations with parties that share similar aspirations, including Bersatu, to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka election. Also present were Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also agriculture and food security minister, and Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa. Meanwhile, Adly, who is also deputy defence minister, said the distribution of seats within PH among PKR, Amanah and DAP had been finalised, including the allocation of eight seats to Amanah.

items.title: MMA calls for tougher enforcement after repeat illegal clinic discoveries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called for tougher enforcement after the latest discovery of suspected illegal clinics and seizure of unregistered medicines and medical equipment. He said the use of unregistered medicines, injections, antibiotics and medical equipment by unqualified or unregistered individuals posed a serious risk to patients and public health. It said inappropriate use of antibiotics could also contribute to antimicrobial resistance.

items.title: 12,575 still waiting for organ transplants as donor numbers rise
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The Health Ministry recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year, up from 89 in 2025, but 12,575 patients remain on the waiting list for new organs as of July. Deputy director-general of health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said the figures, equivalent to about 1.3 deceased donors per million population, showed that public awareness of organ donation had taken root but remained far from satisfactory. Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year's MKPO following encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.

items.title: Malaysia aims to finalise new e-commerce Bill this year, says domestic trade minister
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — The government aims to finalise the drafting of a new e-commerce Bill this year, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. He said the ministry had approved the policy decision to repeal the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 and replace it with a new, more comprehensive law. However, he said the process would require coordination between ministries as well as extensive engagement with stakeholders, including e-commerce platforms, service providers and industry players.

items.title: One-off RM1,000 allowance for Perkeso contributors taking jobs over 100km away
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The government will provide a one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors who secure new jobs located more than 100km from their homes. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said under the Act the allowance would take effect on Oct 1 through amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017. Among the changes is an increase in the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 per cent to 50 per cent of the remaining unpaid Job Search Allowance for eligible workers who return to employment early.

items.title: Malaysia records 102 deceased organ donors so far in 2026, but 12,575 still await transplants, says MOH
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 19 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year. Deputy Director-General of Health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said this is an increase from the 89 deceased organ donors in 2025, equivalent to roughly 1.3 donors per million population. Meanwhile, Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year’s MKPO in light of encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.

items.title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia gets Indonesia’s green light to help battle Kalimantan fires behind haze
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesia has given the green light for Malaysia to assist in tackling forest and land fires in Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto gave his approval during their meeting at Istana Hambalang in conjunction with his working visit to Jakarta. “President Prabowo welcomed the offer, meaning he has given approval for Malaysia to join efforts to address the haze and fires in Kalimantan,” he told a press conference here today.

items.title: Defence Ministry shortlists three missile systems for LCS, says Khaled
items.summary: LUMUT, Sept 19 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) is in the final stage of shortlisting a surface-to-surface missile system from three countries to replace the system for the Royal Malaysian Navy Littoral Combat Ships (LCS). Without disclosing the three countries, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said several issues needed to be finalised before a government decision could be made. Meanwhile, commenting on the possibility of Malaysia acquiring the BrahMos air-to-surface missile system from India, he said the matter would be referred to the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) for study.

items.title: Five students arrested over assault of 14-year-old schoolboy
items.summary: KUANTAN: A businesswoman was left distressed after her 14-year-old son was allegedly assaulted by several senior students using a broomstick at a religious secondary school in Rompin last week. Siti Rohani Yusof said the incident had left her family traumatised, particularly her son, while the alleged lack of action by the school, including its principal and hostel warden, came as a shock. She said her son informed the school management about the incident, but no action was taken.

items.title: RM10 per member: Umno sets RM30mil goal to help Najib pay court fine
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is targeting up to RM30 million for the Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak if all of its estimated 3.8 million members nationwide contribute to the fund. Umno supreme council member Datuk Razlan Rafii said the target was achievable if each member contributed at least RM10. Umno launched the fund to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay a RM50 million fine imposed as a condition of his conditional pardon.

items.title: New MyKad: Dyed hair allowed if not too prominent
items.summary: National Registration Department Identification Card Division director Muhammad Asraf Sukadi said the requirement also took into account an individual's original hair colour, including those with grey hair or who use henna. He said the department did not require applicants to have black hair, but the colour should closely resemble their natural hair colour and not be excessive. "We allow hair colours that are close to the original colour.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution says Home Ministry awaits Pardons Board letter, no Najib house arrest notification yet
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry and Prisons Department had yet to receive the letter from the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department, which serves as the secretariat to the Pardons Board. Saifuddin said the letter would also clarify whether the Pardons Board had specified the premises where Najib would serve his reported house arrest, or whether the matter had been left to the Prisons Department. Currently, Datuk Seri Najib is serving his prison sentence.

items.title: [UPDATED] DAP leaders arrive for emergency CEC meeting over Najib pardon [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and other party leaders have arrived at the DAP headquarters here for an emergency central executive committee (CEC) meeting. Loke arrived at 2.54pm, followed by other leaders, including DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo and Wanita DAP chief Teo Nie Ching. Also spotted arriving for the meeting were DAP deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh, who sits on the Federal Territories Pardons Board, and DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming, as well as other party leaders.

items.title: RTS Link: Border security preparations stepped up ahead of January launch
items.summary: MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods. Shuhaily said MCBA would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks. Meanwhile, Shuhaily said 400 MCBA trainees were undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.

items.title: AKPS steps up border security readiness ahead Johor Bahru‑Singapore RTS Link launch in January
items.summary: AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through the use of technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods. Mohd Shuhaily said AKPS would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks. Meanwhile, Mohd Shuhaily said 400 AKPS trainees were currently undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.

items.title: MACC chief says media key to anti-corruption efforts
items.summary: KAJANG: The media plays a key role in helping the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) combat corruption by delivering accurate and responsible information to the public, its chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said. He said the commission could not fight corruption alone and regarded the media as one of its key strategic partners. Abd Halim was speaking at the MACC Shooting Programme with the Media at Kajang Prison College here today.

items.title: Australian man pleads not guilty to Thai suitcase murder
items.summary: BANGKOK: An Australian accused of murdering a teenage girl in Thailand and abandoning her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty in court on Friday, citing self-defence. The young woman's body was found in a suitcase near a railway track in Pattaya, a seaside resort city south of the capital Bangkok. Carman appeared on Friday at Pattaya Provincial Court, where he denied all charges, citing "self-defence and a mistaken belief about the victim's age", a court statement said.

items.title: Police seek Interpol help after six foreigners charged with Jalan Ampang Pavilion Embassy robbery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Six foreign men were charged in absentia at the Sessions Court here yesterday with armed gang robbery at a residential unit in Pavilion Embassy here on Sept 7. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the charge was framed under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code, which carry a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment and whipping upon conviction. Fadil said the investigation papers were referred to the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Prosecution Office on Sept 17.

items.title: 68,177 people lost jobs between January and Sept 16
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said workers in the manufacturing and wholesale and retail sectors were among those most affected. He said although the figure showed an increase, the labour market remained resilient overall, with the labour force and number of employed people continuing to grow as of July this year. Akmal said the situation showed that the country's labour market remained stable overall, although certain sectors continued to face pressure.

items.title: Preliminary report on Sarawak Flying Doctor helicopter crash due within 30 days, says deputy transport minister
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 19 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (BSKU) will issue a preliminary report on the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash on September 8 within 30 days of the accident, in accordance with Annex 13 of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) on Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation. “BSKU will issue a preliminary report within 30 days from the date of the accident, in accordance with ICAO Annex 13,” he told reporters when met at a function in Long Lama on Saturday (September 19). Hasbi added that the BSKU was currently conducting a technical investigation in accordance with ICAO Annex 13 and Part XXVI of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016.

items.title: Workers to get enhanced EIS benefits, training support from October
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Workers will receive enhanced financial and training support from October, with the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) also expanding employment opportunities and social protection initiatives under a broader effort to strengthen Malaysia's workforce safety net. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said amendments to the Employment Insurance System (EIS) Act, passed by the Dewan Rakyat last December, would improve benefits for contributors who lose their jobs and strengthen the system's governance. The amendments also strengthen Perkeso's role in providing employment services, including job matching, career counselling and other active labour market programmes.

items.title: Prabowo welcomes Malaysia's offer to assist in tackling Indonesia forest fires
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has welcomed Malaysia's offer to assist in tackling forest fires in the country, including through the provision of assets and expertise. He said the offer involved an aircraft, three helicopters and a firefighting team. Prabowo said Indonesia had also received offers of assistance from several other countries, including Japan, to help put out the prolonged forest fires, particularly in Kalimantan.

items.title: PH Presidential Council discussed house arrest, not GE16, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: MELAKA: The Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council meeting yesterday focused on the legal and procedural aspects of implementing house arrest, says Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said house arrest was a new concept in Malaysia and its implementation needed to be carefully studied from legal and operational perspectives. What was discussed was how to handle this new situation regarding house arrest," said Mohamad, who is commonly known as Mat Sabu.

items.title: Cloud seeding operation begins in Klang Valley after API readings exceed 150 for 24 hours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The government, through the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), will conduct a cloud seeding operation in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya today and tomorrow to mitigate the effects of the haze and improve air quality in the affected areas. Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the operation was being carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department, Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), with an RMAF C-130 Hercules aircraft serving as the main asset. “The cloud seeding operation is scheduled to be conducted on Sept 19 and 20, following Air Pollutant Index (API) readings for PM2.5 in the affected areas exceeding 150 for more than 24 hours, based on readings by the Department of Environment.

items.title: Malaysia to study proposal for India's BrahMos missile system
items.summary: LUMUT: Malaysia will study a proposal to acquire India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. He said the proposal, which was raised during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's recent visit to India, would first be studied by the Royal Malaysian Air Force. He said the assessment would also consider the implications of integrating the proposed missile system with existing equipment, including whether upgrades would be required for the Sukhoi fighter jets.

items.title: PH will contest Melaka election regardless of cooperation outcome, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUANTAN: There has yet to be any decision on potential political cooperation for the Melaka election, but Pakatan Harapan (PH) will contest the polls regardless of the outcome. PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the coalition was ready to enter the election battleground and face its opponents in the Melaka state election. "No decision has been made regarding political cooperation for the Melaka state election, but the fight goes on.

items.title: Melaka Pakatan finalising talks with Bersatu, others to form PH Plus for state polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 19 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) Melaka is finalising negotiations with parties that have similar aspirations, including Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka State Election. Also present were Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, and Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa. Meanwhile, Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister, said the distribution of seats within PH among PKR, Amanah and DAP had been finalised, including the allocation of eight seats to Amanah.

items.title: Brazil police nab suspected serial killer disguised as woman
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazilian police said Friday they had captured a suspected serial killer linked to at least 16 deaths since May, who was arrested while disguised as a woman and carrying a baby. The suspect was arrested Sunday after a 30-hour police manhunt in a forested area of Paraiba state in northeastern Brazil. "Although the suspect claimed involvement in 80 homicides, civil police have confirmed his participation in 16 killings in the region, 11 of which he confessed to during questioning," police told AFP.

items.title: Prabowo welcomes Malaysia’s offer of aircraft, helicopters and team to fight Indonesia fires
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has welcomed Malaysia’s offer to assist in tackling forest fires in the country, including through the provision of assets and expertise. He said the offer involved an aircraft, three helicopters and a firefighting team. Prabowo said Indonesia had also received offers of assistance from several other countries, including Japan, to help put out the prolonged forest fires, particularly in Kalimantan.

items.title: Israeli, Lebanese armies face off after Israeli advance in south Lebanon
items.summary: DEÏR MIMASS, Lebanon: Israel's military moved forward on Friday in a south Lebanon village, facing off against a Lebanese army position and detonating stun grenades, Lebanon's army and an AFP photographer said. Israel has been occupying a swathe of south Lebanon since war broke out in March against Lebanese group Hizbollah, but the Lebanese army is supposed to gradually take control of the area under a framework agreement between the two countries. But the Lebanese army has stayed out of hostilities between Israel and Hizbollah.

items.title: Home Ministry, Prisons Dept await Pardons Board letter on Najib's house arrest
items.summary: KULIM: The Home Ministry and Prisons Department have yet to receive an official letter from the Pardons Board on the conditional house arrest granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry would wait for formal notification of the board's decision before determining its next course of action. Currently, Datuk Seri Najib is serving his prison sentence.

items.title: MIC's Sivaraj seeks clarity on 30 pct Bumiputera equity rule for tuition centres
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MIC National Strategic Director Datuk C. Sivaraj has called on the Education Ministry to clarify the proposed 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for tuition centres. The rule would require tuition centres to have at least 30 per cent Bumiputera equity, with implications for existing operators from 2027. Sivaraj said efforts to increase Bumiputera participation in the economy should not come at the expense of the rights and equity of non-Bumiputera communities through licensing conditions, rulings or administrative regulations.

items.title: Trump: Son to repay Russian oligarch who funded wedding parties
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Friday his son, Donald Trump Jr., has told him he would pay back a Russian oligarch who bankrolled wedding celebrations for him in the Bahamas in May. Democrats in the US Congress launched an investigation ‌this week into reports that Umar Kremlev, a wealthy Russian businessman and president of the International Boxing Association, paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the wedding festivities. ProPublica, which first reported Kremlev's involvement, said he has close ties to the Russian government.

items.title: Child assault case: Don't paint all soldiers with same brush, says Khaled
items.summary: Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said such incidents were not confined to military personnel and could also occur among members of the public. Khaled said the armed forces would continue to pay attention to such cases and provide the necessary guidance and advice to its personnel. Khaled said the armed forces would continue to provide guidance, counselling and advice where necessary.

items.title: Helicopters battle wildfire threatening Ecuador's capital Quito
items.summary: QUITO: Ecuadoran firefighters backed by helicopters on Friday battled a major blaze on a hill overlooking the capital Quito that has led to the evacuation of dozens of people. On the ground, around 100 firefighters were fighting to contain two hotspots, Captain Pablo Andino of the Quito Fire Department told AFP. Quito Mayor Pabel Munoz estimated the area consumed by flames on Casitagua at around 100 hectares.

items.title: Government shortlists three missile systems for navy's LCS
items.summary: LUMUT: The government has shortlisted three surface-to-surface missile (SSM) systems from three countries for the Royal Malaysian Navy's Littoral Combat Ships (LCS). Khaled said three types of SSMs had been shortlisted. "Three... three types of surface-to-surface missiles," he said when asked about the number of companies shortlisted.

items.title: PM Anwar vows to strengthen pondok schools, introduce AI and modern fields
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 19 — The government will help streamline and elevate pondok institutions (traditional religious schools), including in terms of physical facilities, academic disciplines and the introduction of new fields of study suited to current needs, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The Prime Minister said that, as an initial step, several pondok institutions would be selected to pioneer new traditions of learning based on their respective areas of specialisation and tarbiah or disciplines. So children in pondok institutions must also be trained to master AI,” he said.

items.title: Kedah fertiliser probe: Mohamad Sabu confirms giving MACC statement
items.summary: MELAKA: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu has confirmed that he had his statement recorded by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist in an investigation into alleged irregularities and delays in the supply of fertiliser in Kedah. Mohamad, who is also Amanah president, said he spent about 30 minutes giving his statement to MACC over its investigation into the delayed distribution of Additional Compound Fertiliser. Also present were Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof; Amanah vice-presidents Datuk Mahfuz Omar and Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad; and Amanah Melaka chairman Adly Zahari.

items.title: MACC says Najib’s conditional pardon has no impact on 1MDB case
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 19 — The status of the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case involving Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak remains unchanged following his conditional pardon, said Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. He said each case must be handled separately based on the issues and investigations involved. Abd Halim said one case could not simply be equated with another, as each investigation involved different allegations and issues.

items.title: MYSA defence intelligence application director appointed to lead armed forces cyber force team
items.summary: LUMUT: Brigadier-General Datuk Abd Razak Sipit has been appointed head of the armed forces Cyber Force Nucleus Team, marking the first step towards establishing the country's fourth military service by 2030. The nucleus team will study and develop the requirements for establishing the Cyber Force, which will complement the existing Army, Navy and Air Force. Khaled said the new service was necessary as modern warfare had evolved beyond conventional battlefields, with security threats increasingly taking non-traditional and hybrid forms.

items.title: Perodua Alza driver dies after collision with Volvo trailer lorry near Sungai Tong in Terengganu
items.summary: BANDAR PERMAISURI, Sept 19 — A man was killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) he was driving collided with a trailer lorry at Kilometre 38 of Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu near Sungai Tong here last night. Setiu district police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the accident at 12.01am and identified the victim as Mohd Assfarizal Salim, 44, of Taman Balok Pelangi, Kuantan, Pahang. Zahril Asri said the lorry driver, who was travelling from Jertih to Kuantan, was uninjured, adding that police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

items.title: Haze: Cloud seeding operation in KL, Putrajaya, Selangor today and tomorrow, says Nadma
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A cloud seeding operation will be conducted today and tomorrow to reduce the impact of haze in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Selangor. Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the cloud seeding operation was being conducted following PM2.5 readings in the affected areas exceeding 150 for more than 24 hours, based on readings issued by the Department of Environment (DoE). According to the DoE's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), air quality monitoring stations in Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur and Selangor were among 17 stations that recorded unhealthy API readings as of 1pm today.

items.title: Google's Gemini AI carried out cyberattacks, guessed passwords
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Google's consumer AI model Gemini hacked multiple systems through guessing login credentials, the company told AFP on Friday, the latest case of rogue AI cybersecurity transgressions, which have generated safety concerns. "In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test," Heather Adkins, Google's vice president of security engineering, told AFP in a statement. "These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly," Adkins emphasised.--AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: New RM270,000 fishing hall for Tanjung Bidara community
items.summary: Amir Mamat Pix - Amir Mamat MASJID TANAH: Fishermen in Kampung Pasir Gembur, Tanjung Bidara, will receive a new RM270,000 fishing hall next month, courtesy of Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Pasir Gembur Fishermen Association chairman Rusli Othman said the commitment ends a decade-long wait for a modern facility. He said the new hall will streamline daily operations for 27 local fishermen, from preparing their gear to landing their daily catch.

items.title: MACC records Mat Sabu’s statement in fertiliser supply probe, 37 witnesses called so far
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recorded statements from Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and the ministry’s secretary-general in connection with an investigation into the delays in the supply of fertiliser in Kedah. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Mohamad’s statement was recorded on September 16, while the secretary-general’s statement was recorded a day earlier. He added that, so far, 37 witnesses had been called and their statements recorded to assist in the investigation, which began on August 26, regarding the appointment of a company by the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM).

items.title: MACC directs former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez and family to file asset declarations within one month
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission (MACC) has issued notices to former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim and his family members requiring them to declare their assets within a month. According to Berita Harian (BH), MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the notices were handed to Azeez and his children this week under legal provisions. “We have already served notices on Datuk Seri Azeez and his family to declare their assets within a month as provided under the law.

items.title: Three young motorcyclists killed, nine injured as 15 vehicles collide in pre‑dawn Ipoh crash
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 19 — Three motorcyclists were killed and nine others injured in a crash involving 12 motorcycles and three cars along Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here early today. Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the incident was reported at 3.35am, Harian Metro (HM) reported. All three car drivers escaped injury.

items.title: MCMC and police trace individuals tied to resurfaced 2018 clip accused of insulting Rukun Negara
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 19 —The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has identified several social media accounts and individuals linked to a viral video of a stage performance that allegedly insults the institution of the Malay Rulers and the Rukun Negara. In a statement today, MCMC said an initial review found that the recording originated from a 2018 stage performance and has since resurfaced on social media. “MCMC is also working with the Criminal Investigation Department of the Royal Malaysia Police to complete the investigation, including matters related to digital evidence,” the statement read.

items.title: Thumbprints gave her away: Woman gets four months’ jail for presenting fake MyKad at Sabah NRD
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 19 — A 55-year-old woman who went to the Sabah National Registration Department (NRD) to replace her identity card ended up being arrested after the card was found to be fake. Jamilah Akrim was sentenced to four months’ jail by Magistrate Dzul Elmy Yunus after pleading guilty to possessing the fake identity card at the Sabah NRD Identity Card Division at about 11.30am on Sept 10. The court also ordered Jamilah to be referred to the Immigration Department for further action upon completing her sentence.

items.title: Azalina: Pardon power is part of the law, not above it
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The constitutional power to grant pardons should not be portrayed as placing any individual above the law, Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today. She said the power of pardon was expressly provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution and was therefore not a power exercised outside the law. Respect the Constitution.

items.title: Five hours, one lorry: Civil Defence, villagers pull together to bury 23-year-old, 250kg man in Rantau Panjang
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) today assisted with the burial of a 250-kilogramme man at the Gual Tinggi Islamic Cemetery in Rantau Panjang. Rantau Panjang APM officer Lt (PA) Mohd Fuad Ismail said the team received a request from the Ministry of Health early this morning to undertake the special service. — Bernama * Editor’s note: The initials APM stand for Angkatan Pertahanan Awam Malaysia.

items.title: Prison Dept vehicles enter Najib’s home as preparations for house arrest appear to begin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Two vehicles bearing the Prison Department logo were seen entering the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak at Jalan Langgak Duta here this morning. Plainclothes personnel walk along the perimeter of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence at Jalan Langgak Duta in Kuala Lumpur on September 19, 2026. Plainclothes personnel are seen near the perimeter of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence at Jalan Langgak Duta in Kuala Lumpur on September 19, 2026.

items.title: Isa Samad gives statement from Sungai Buloh Prison as MACC widens Felda probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is recording former Felda chairman Datuk Isa Samad’s statement at Sungai Buloh Prison as part of investigations into Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC). MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said investigators began recording Isa’s statement on September 17 and continued yesterday, adding that the process is expected to continue for another three or four days, The New Straits Times reported. The statement is being recorded as MACC intensifies investigations into seven cases involving the purchase or investment in assets by Felda and FIC between 2010 and 2020.

items.title: Lubok Antu haze worsens as API climbs to 178 in eight hours
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 19 — Air quality in Lubok Antu deteriorated as its Air Pollutant Index (API) rose to 178 by 8am on Saturday, from 106 at 10pm the previous day. According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s API Status for Sarawak, Sri Aman, Lundu and Tebedu also recorded increases in API readings. The API in Sri Aman, Lundu and Tebedu stood at 161, 157 and 119, respectively, by 8am.

items.title: Haze stretches from Tawau to Perak as 20 areas record unhealthy air, Kuching and Serian hit 169
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — As of 9am today, 20 areas nationwide are recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. Two areas in Perak logged unhealthy readings: Seri Manjung (164) and Tanjung Malim (113). Meanwhile, 37 areas recorded moderate readings, while another 10 areas registered good readings.

items.title: Padang Besar police bust suspected Vellfire insurance scam, arrest four including civil servant
items.summary: Padang Besar police chief ACP Mohd Shokri Abdullah said the suspects, aged between 32 and 45, were arrested in raids at three locations in the Padang Besar and Arau districts at about 5.15pm Thursday. He said the main suspect, a 42-year-old civil servant in Perlis, had travelled to Kuala Lumpur on July 16 to attend a course, using his wife’s black Toyota Vellfire. Mohd Shokri said investigations found that the reported loss was believed to have been staged by the main suspect and his 45-year-old brother to facilitate an insurance claim.

items.title: Where did Tasik Bera’s forest go? Pahang probes suspected illegal clearing of 7,000ha for crops
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 19 — The Pahang State Enforcement Unit (UPNP) suspects that more than 7,000 hectares of the Tasik Bera Permanent Forest Reserve have been illegally cleared for commercial crops such as oil palm and rubber. UPNP chief Saifullah Muhammad Ali said the matter was detected during integrated enforcement operations carried out in the area since Sept 14, involving 160 officers and personnel from UPNP, the Pahang State Forestry Department, the Pahang Department of Wildlife and National Parks, and the Bera District and Land Office. “In addition, we also obtained security assistance from the Bera district police and the General Operations Force 7th Battalion,” he said.

items.title: Anwar urges Malaysians to manage energy use as haze worsens, says govt seeking solutions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on the people to play their part in addressing the increasingly worrying haze situation, while the government continues to seek solutions in the interest of all. The prime minister also urged the public to use energy wisely. Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan called on all mosques and surau nationwide to hold special prayers and offer supplications for Allah SWT’s protection from the haze affecting the country.

items.title: Four men, a folding knife and RM30,000: Police probe alleged gang robbery near Sungai Petani courthouse
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Sept 19 — A 22-year-old man claimed he was robbed of RM30,000 in company funds by four men in an incident yesterday. Kuala Muda District Police Chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said preliminary investigations indicated that the incident occurred at about 4.30pm yesterday near the Sungai Petani Court Complex here. “However, the victim only lodged a police report at the Sungai Petani Police Station at about 7am today.
